										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/hottea-3.jpg" alt="August 2026 Opportunities: Open Calls, Residencies, and Grants for Artists" />


<p>Every month, we share opportunities for artists and designers, including open calls, grants, fellowships, and residencies. Make sure you never miss out by joining our monthly&nbsp;<a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/newsletter/opportunities/">Opportunities Newsletter</a>.</p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.exhibizone.com/nuditas?SCH=75801" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Nuditas 2026: 5th Annual Juried Exhibition, Publication, Promotion, and Sales</a><span style="background-color: #ffdc13; padding: 2px 6px; margin-left: 8px; font-size: .9em; font-style: italic;"><strong>Featured</strong></span></strong><br>Ready to reveal the naked truth of the human body? From personal identity and body positivity to spirituality, mythology, emotion, and vulnerability, Nuditas 2026 celebrates the human form in all its expressions. Submit your strongest figurative or abstract works for the opportunity to exhibit internationally, be featured on Artsy, published in the official catalogue, and promoted worldwide.<br>Learn more and submit: <a href="https://www.exhibizone.com/nuditas?SCH=75801" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">www.exhibizone.com/nuditas</a><br><strong><em>Deadline: 11:59 p.m. PST on August 13, 2026</em></strong>.</p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.archenemyarts.com/opencall" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Arch Enemy Arts Call for Artists</a><span style="background-color: #ffdc13; padding: 2px 6px; margin-left: 8px; font-size: .9em; font-style: italic;"><strong>Featured</strong></span></strong><br>Arch Enemy Arts is seeking submissions for an annual group exhibition in January 2027. This spotlight exhibition of new and emerging talent has no themes or direction in subject matter, although the gallery focuses on representational, dark surrealism, magical realism, post-graffiti, pop-surrealism, narrative, illustrative, and figurative work across a range of artistic mediums. The exhibition is open to artists worldwide, who are invited to submit up to three works for consideration.<br><strong><em>Deadline: 11:59 p.m. EST on November 13, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p>&nbsp;</p>



<p><strong><strong style="font-size: 1.2em;">Open Calls</strong></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.thebritishartprize.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">The British Art Prize</a></strong> <em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>The British Art Prize, run by <em>Artists &amp; Illustrators</em> magazine, is one of the U.K.’s most exciting annual art competitions showcasing the talent and diversity of contemporary artists from around the world. Each year, a panel of leading curators, gallerists, and art professionals selects a shortlist of outstanding works. These finalists are exhibited at London’s Oxo Gallery. Winners are awarded prizes worth more than £10,000, including cash awards, art materials, a solo exhibition at Panter &amp; Hall’s Cecil Court Gallery, and editorial features in <em>Artists &amp; Illustrators</em>.<br><strong><em>Deadline: 5 p.m. BST on August 7, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.codaworx.com/rfq/detail/xx" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Clotilda Memorial Alabama Historical Commission</a></strong>&nbsp;<em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>The Alabama Historical Commission is seeking proposals to honor the last known African captives trafficked to the United States through the transatlantic slave trade: the <a href="https://theclotildamemorial.info/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Clotilda</a> survivors. The memorial will convey dimensions of the survivors’ lives and legacies—celebrating their resilient and determined spirits amidst violent dislocation, enslavement, and discrimination. Projects will be developed through a collaborative process that will engage the community founded by the Clotilda survivors and other formerly enslaved people: historic Africatown and the expansive diaspora. The total budget is $2,000,000.<br><strong><em>Deadline: 11:59 p.m. CDT on August 9, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><strong><a href="http://artistonish.com/calls?SCH=97101" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Publish Your Art in <em>Artistonish </em>Magazine and Sell on Artsy</a></strong></strong><em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>Submit works of art for the 73rd issue of <em>Artistonish</em> Contemporary Art Magazine, featuring juried contemporary works online and on premium glossy print pages. Each selected artwork receives a full-page image, dedicated QR code, Artsy feature for sales visibility, certificate of achievement, exclusive artwork badges, global promotion, and lasting online presence within the international art community. There is no fee to apply; selected artists pay a selection fee of $45.<br><strong><em>Deadline: 11:59 p.m. PDT on August 11, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.thewildcanvasretreat.art/sketch-contest" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">The Wild Canvas Sketch Challenge to Win a Puerto Rico Art Retreat</a></strong><em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>The Wild Canvas is organizing its inaugural art retreat in Ceiba, Puerto Rico, which invites up to 12 artists for a week-long program in January 2027. A sketching contest around the theme of &#8220;Island Time&#8221; provides a chance to win a fully funded spot, plus additional scholarships.<br><em style="font-weight: bold;"><strong>Deadline: August 25, 2026.</strong></em></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://spruillarts.org/amplify/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">AMPLIFY Mural Open Call</a></strong><em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(U.S.)</mark></em></em><br>The Spruill Gallery in Dunwoody, Georgia, is accepting nationwide submissions for its annual AMPLIFY mural competition. The winning artist will receive a $10,000 prize, and their mural will adorn the side of the historic Spruill Smoke House for the coming year.<br><em style="font-weight: bold;"><strong>Deadline: 11:59 p.m. EDT on August 28, 2026.</strong></em></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScrqxHab5NmFYGLgAXOWfejyt3jnPgcRBI6CeLusz1dzPu-YQ/viewform" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">ARTLittle 1st International Metaverse Art Expo</a> </strong><em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>The 1st International Metaverse Art Expo, presented by ARTLittle, is a 3D multiuser online exhibition where visitors from around the world walk through the galleries with avatars, discover artworks, and buy directly. ARTLittle is an independent art project built in Malaysia and is open to artists and galleries worldwide. Three hundred artists will be selected for exhibition in the virtual expo and have works offered for sale.<br><strong><em>Deadline: 11:59 p.m. MYT on August 31, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.huntmuseum.com/whats-on/hunt-museum-open-submission-exhibition-2026/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Hunt Museum Open Submission Exhibition</a></strong> <em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>The Hunt Open Submission Exhibition is an initiative celebrating contemporary Irish and international art at the Hunt Museum in Limerick. There is a €15 entry fee for the first image, plus an additional €15 per artwork for up to three submissions.<br><strong><em>Deadline: September 7, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.hidinginplainsite.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Hiding in Plain Site: <strong>International Public Art Short Film Festival</strong></a></strong> <em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>HPS invites filmmakers, artists, and creative practitioners to submit short works between two and 20 minutes for consideration in this screening program, which will premiere on October 25 in Minneapolis. HPS seeks to bring together film, video art, experimental media, XR (extended reality), and other works that expand how public art is experienced and represented. <br><strong><em>Deadline: September 10, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.mendocinoartcenter.org/teach" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Apply to Teach at Mendocino Art Center</a></strong> <em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(U.S.)</mark></em><br>The Mendocino Art Center (MAC), located in the coastal Northern California community of Mendocino, offers workshops taught by both visiting and local artists in a wide variety of mediums and topics. Some instructors choose to be compensated, and some choose to teach pro bono to help MAC offer more affordable workshops.<br><strong><em>Deadline: Rolling.</em></strong></p>



<p>&nbsp;</p>



<p><strong><strong style="font-size: 1.2em;">Grants</strong></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.bigfieldfund.org/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Big Fields Fund Grants for Eastern Iowa Artists</a></strong> <em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(Iowa)</mark></em><br>The Big Field Fund awards grants to artists and collectives to support publicly-engaged experimental, collaborative, and connective visual arts projects in eastern Iowa. Project grants award $8,000 to support the public realization of artist-led projects, while research and development grants offer $3,000 to support artists in the early stages of an ambitious project.<br><strong><em>Deadline: August 1, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://skogart.org/blog/5haqp3iqd3tkygl6iponogv3fyl8bx" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">SKOG Art Space Exhibitions Open Call</a></strong> <em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em><br>This open call welcomes artists from around the world at all career stages to apply for both solo and group exhibitions at SKOG in Oslo, Norway. The gallery welcomes proposals from both emerging and established artists working across all media and techniques.<br><strong><em>Deadline: August 16, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://artsmidwest.org/get-support/midwest-culture-bearers-award/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Midwest Culture Bearers Award</a></strong> <em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(Midwest)</mark></em><br>The Midwest Culture Bearers Award honors and amplifies the work of 18 mid-career and established Midwestern cultural practitioners each year. Selected individuals will each receive a $5,000 unrestricted award. No cost share or match is required to receive these funds. Additionally, Arts Midwest offers awardees virtual professional development and networking opportunities, plus the opportunity to have a story written about their work.<br><strong><em>Deadline: August 18, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.anchorlightraleigh.com/brightwork-grants" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">2027 Brightwork Fellowship &amp; Grants</a></strong> <em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(North Carolina)</mark></em><br>Anchorlight, based in Raleigh, offers one fellowship and two grants for 2027. The Professional Development Grant amounts to $2,000, and the Studio Project Grant awards $3,000. The fellowship is a year-long program geared toward an artist who is at a pivotal point in their career, providing a 500+ square-foot studio space at Anchorlight, an exhibition opportunity in its gallery, and an unrestricted financial award of $50,000. One artist will be selected for each, and each must have lived in North Carolina for at least 12 months as of applying. There is a $10 application fee for each opportunity.<br><strong><em>Deadline: August 28, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><a href="https://www.jracraft.org/chrysalis-award.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener"><strong>2026 Chrysalis Award for Emerging Ceramic Artists</strong></a> <em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(U.S.)</mark></em></em><br>The Chrysalis Award was created by the James Renwick Alliance for Craft to support and inspire emerging craft artists in the United States. Eligible applicants are in the early stages of their professional artistic careers—regardless of age—and have completed their training within the past five years. This year’s award will recognize an emerging artist working in ceramics, who will receive a $5,000 unrestricted award, a one-year JRACraft membership, and the opportunity to present their work at a JRACraft event.<br><strong><em>Deadline: August 23, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.lsmartfund.org/grants" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Liu Shiming Artist Grants</a></strong> <em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(U.S.)</mark></em></em><br>Designed to support the work of visual artists during the first decade of their careers, the Liu Shiming Artist Grants support the creation or completion of new projects that explore the interplay between traditional cultural or historical influences and contemporary artistic practice. Up to five artists will be selected to receive a $5,000 grant.<br><strong><em>Deadline: August 31, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.dezi.work/artprize" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Dezi Art Prize</a></strong> <em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>This global juried art grant is geared toward emerging and early-career visual artists. Two winners each receive a $1,000 unrestricted grant, plus a featured profile. Ten finalists are named and featured. Open worldwide, all visual media is welcome, with entries scored on merit by an independent jury. There is a $30 application fee.<br><strong><em>Deadline: September 10, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.printedmatter.org/workgrant" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Printed Matter Publisher Work Grant</a></strong> <em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>Now in its third year, Printed Matter&#8217;s Publisher Work Grant program offers funding to independent presses with a history of artists’ book publishing, acknowledging awardees’ accomplishments in past work and providing the capacity-building funds to enable future book projects and publisher sustainability. In 2026, three unrestricted grants of $10,000 will be awarded to three independent artists’ book publishers. Printed Matter will also extend a featured exhibitor presence at a forthcoming Printed Matter NY or LA Art Book Fair to selected presses.<br><strong><em>Deadline: October 4, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://arrivalgallery.myflodesk.com/arrival-grant" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">ARRIVAL Gallery Micro Grant</a></strong>&nbsp;<em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>The ARRIVAL Grant is designed to keep support simple and accessible. Artists submit one original artwork to the current round, and once the round reaches 1,000 valid submissions, one eligible artist receives a&nbsp;£100 grant&nbsp;and a new round begins.<br><em><strong>Deadline: Rolling.</strong></em></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.gottliebfoundation.org/emergency-grant" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">The Adolf and Esther Gottlieb Emergency Grant</a></strong>&nbsp;<em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>This program provides one-time financial assistance to qualified painters, printmakers, and sculptors whose needs resulted from an unforeseen catastrophic incident and who lack the resources to meet that situation. Awardees typically receive $5,000 and up to $15,000.<br><em><strong>Deadline: Rolling.</strong></em></p>



<p><a href="https://pkf.org/apply/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener"><strong>Pollock-Krasner Foundation Grant</strong></a><em>&nbsp;<em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>The foundation welcomes applications from painters, sculptors, and artists working on paper, including printmakers. Grants are intended for one year and range up to $50,000. The artist’s circumstances determine the size of the grant, and professional exhibition history will be considered.<br><em><strong>Deadline: Rolling.</strong></em></p>



<p>&nbsp;</p>



<p><strong style="font-size: 1.2em;">Residencies, Fellowships, &amp; More</strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://bigci.org/awards/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">BigCi Environmental Awards 2026</a></strong> <em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>Australian and international artists working in visual art, installation, multimedia, performance, literature, music, photography, filmmaking, and curating are invited to submit entries for the BigCi Environmental Awards 2026. Two winning artists will each receive a free four-week residency at BigCi, where they will have the opportunity to explore the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Wollemi, Blue Mountains, and Gardens of Stone National Parks in Australia. The winners also receive an AUD$5,000 award. There is an AUD$40 application fee.<br><em style="font-weight: bold;"><strong>Deadline: August 2, 2026.</strong></em></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://tada-residency.ch/en/residence" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">TaDA Residency 2027</a></strong> <em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>Each year, six jury-selected candidates have the opportunity to work with textile companies in Eastern Switzerland, use a local studio in Arbon, and extend their individual networks over a period of three months. At the <em>TaDA Spinnerei</em> event, also attended by international speakers, artists can present their projects to an interested public and discuss with experts.<br><strong style="font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;">Deadline: August 12, 2026.</strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.surfacedesign.org/air_form/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Surface Design Association Artist-in-Residence Program</a></strong> <em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>The residency program facilitated by the Surface Design Association (SDA) is designed to build skills, leverage relationships, and offer support to early, mid-career, and established fiber artists as they undertake studio projects that inspire artistic growth. The residency is virtual, and the selected participant is provided with a $2,000 studio stipend to support projects during their time. There is no application fee, but applicants must be members of SDA.<br><strong style="font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;">Deadline: August 14, 2026.</strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.cprnyc.org/events/opencall-2027airprogram" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Center for Performance Research AiR</a></strong> <em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(New York City)</mark></em></em><br>CPR&#8217;s residency supports artists working in contemporary dance, performance, and time-based art. The organization values experimental approaches to content, form, and aesthetics and encourages risk-taking, interdisciplinarity, and the unexpected. The residency runs for one year (January to December 2027) and includes a $2,000 stipend, 20 free hours of rehearsal space, and more.<br><strong style="font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;">Deadline: 5 p.m. EDT on August 24, 2026.</strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.beamarts.gr/international-artist-residency" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">bEam arts Residency</a></strong> <em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>bEam arts is an independent, artist-led residency program located in Thessaloniki, Greece, which welcomes visual artists and writers. The program supports a vibrant studio practice for up to four visual artists and two writers to stay for one or two months. During the residency, bEam arts hosts monthly activities and provides artists with opportunities to connect, engage with one another, and expand their professional networks.&nbsp;Each cycle ends with a group exhibition. The cost is €1,850 per month, including accommodation.<br><strong style="font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;">Deadline: August 24, 2026.</strong></p>



<p><a href="https://www.barca13.pt/en/avistavulcao/agora/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener"><strong>AVISTAVULCÃO</strong> <strong>Residency</strong></a> <em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(Europe)</mark></em></em><br>Part of the Culture Moves Europe initiative, this open call is for applications for a one-month artist-in-residence program focused on research and creation, to take place in March 2027, intended for an artist or artistic duo. Located on the Azares island of Faial, near the Capelinhos Volcano, the residency offers an immersion in a territory shaped by the power of geology, its insular nature, and the constant interplay between nature and human presence. <br><strong style="font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;">Deadline: August 31, 2026.</strong></p>



<p><a href="https://helpmannacademy.com.au/helpmann-fellowships/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener"><strong>Helpmann Fellowships</strong> </a><em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(South Australia)</mark></em></em><br>Three Helpmann Fellowships of up to AUD $7,500 are available to support ambitious, self-directed projects that advance the artistic and professional development of recent graduates (within five years) of eligible performing and visual arts programs at South Australia&#8217;s two universities. Funding can support larger-scale creative projects, tailored professional development, or a combination of both.<br><strong style="font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;">Deadline: 11:59 p.m. ACST on August 31, 2026.</strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.listasafn.is/en/art/news-vasulka-stofa/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">2027 National Gallery of Iceland Residency</a></strong><em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color"><em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em></mark></em></em><br>The National Gallery of Iceland is seeking applications to its CUSP program, a European cooperation project funded through Creative Europe’s Culture grant. Artists working in complex media or emerging technologies are invited to apply. The residency will be up to four weeks long, and accommodation, workspace, and stipends are provided.<br><strong style="font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;">Deadline: 11:59 p.m. GMT on September 2, 2026.</strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://artssoutheast.org/onview-residency-app" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">ON::View Artist Residency Program</a></strong><em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>Located in the heart of Savannah’s Starland District at ARTS Southeast, the fully-funded ON::View Artist Residency provides a free, high-visibility studio space, lodging, and a $500 stipend for an artist or curator to complete a new project, continue an in-progress endeavor, or to conduct research. There is a $50 application fee.<br><strong><em>Deadline: 11:59 p.m. ET on September 7, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.macdowell.org/apply/apply-for-fellowship" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">MacDowell Fellowships for Spring/Summer 2027</a></strong><em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>Located in Peterborough, New Hampshire, MacDowell encourages applications from artists of all backgrounds and all countries in the following disciplines: architecture, film/video, interdisciplinary arts, literature, music composition, theatre, and visual arts. A Fellowship consists of exclusive use of a private studio, accommodations, and three prepared meals a day for two to eight weeks.<br><strong style="font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;">Deadline: September 10, 2026.</strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://queensmuseum.org/program/open-call-2027-28-qm-jerome-foundation-fellowship-for-emerging-artists/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">2027-28 QM-Jerome Foundation Fellowship for Emerging Artists</a></strong><em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(New York City)</mark></em></em><br>The Queens Museum (QM) launches its eighth iteration of the QM-Jerome Foundation Fellowship for Emerging Artists in New York City. Two visual artists will receive $20,000 each and professional development consultations from QM staff members working toward an artist’s project. Each fellow will also receive mentorship from a New York-based established artist. The fellowships will culminate in solo project exhibitions at the Queens Museum in 2028. The duration of each fellowship is one year, culminating with the opening of the fellow’s exhibition.<br><strong style="font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;">Deadline: 11:59 p.m. EDT on September 28, 2026.</strong></p>



<p><a href="https://quarantinemenorca.events/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener"><strong>Quarantine</strong></a> <em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>Dubbed &#8220;purgatory for artists,&#8221; Quarantine is a week-long intensive art program on an 18th-century quarantine island off the coast of Menorca, Spain. The program is open to beginners and professionals alike and offers three 45-minute private mentorships throughout the week, with activities lasting 12+ hours per day. Phones are banned.<br><strong><em>Deadline: Rolling.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://residenciacorazon.com.ar/artist-residency-program-argentina-residencia-corazon/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Residencia Corazón</a></strong> <em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>Residencia Corazón is an independent, artist-run residency in La<br>Plata, Argentina—a home for artists since 2006. The program welcomes visual<br>artists, writers, curators, and creative researchers from around the<br>world for one- to three-month residencies. Each stay is fully personalized, and fees range from $800 to $1,500 per month.<br><strong><em>Deadline: Rolling.</em></strong></p>

		<item>
		<title>Innovation Meets Heritage in West African Contemporary Artists&#8217; Masquerade Ensembles</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/new-african-masquerades-exhibition-west-africa-masks-costumes-traditions/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Kate Mothes]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Wed, 29 Jul 2026 15:47:30 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[History]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Africa]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[costumes]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Indigenous culture]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[masks]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[performance]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[spirituality]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=476246</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-8.jpeg" alt="Innovation Meets Heritage in West African Contemporary Artists&#8217; Masquerade Ensembles" />'New African Masquerades: Artistic Innovations and Collaborations' celebrates contemporary creations by artists in Nigeria, Burkina Faso, Sierra Leone, and Cameroon.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/new-african-masquerades-exhibition-west-africa-masks-costumes-traditions/">Innovation Meets Heritage in West African Contemporary Artists&#8217; Masquerade Ensembles</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-8.jpeg" alt="Innovation Meets Heritage in West African Contemporary Artists&#8217; Masquerade Ensembles" />


<p>Across West Africa, Indigenous communities mark holidays, rites, and sacred events with a remarkable variety of ceremonies ranging from dances to processions. These <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masquerade_ceremony" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">masquerade traditions</a> incorporate meticulously carved masks and full-body costumes that often facilitate links between humans and the spiritual world. There&#8217;s evidence of masked customs dating back millennia, and today, artists continue the tradition of hand-hewn masks and ensembles in vivid colors and a wide array of materials—sometimes with a twist.</p>



<p>The exhibition <em>New African Masquerades: Artistic Innovations and Collaborations</em>, which opens at the <a href="https://mfastpete.org/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Museum of Fine Arts St. Petersburg</a> next month, celebrates contemporary creations by four artists: Chief Ekpenyong Bassey Nsa (Nigeria), David Sanou (Burkina Faso), Sheku “Goldenfinger” Fofanah (Sierra Leone), and Hervé Youmbi (Cameroon). Along with displays of some of their masks and full ensembles, visitors will be able to explore documentary photographs and videos of ceremonies and parades in addition to immersive multimedia experiences.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2667" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-5.jpeg" alt="a geometric mask and colorful raffia costume of an African masquerade ensemble" class="wp-image-476254" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-5.jpeg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-5-640x853.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-5-960x1280.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-5-768x1024.jpeg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-5-1152x1536.jpeg 1152w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-5-1536x2048.jpeg 1536w" sizes="(max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Headpiece by André Sanou and body by anonymous artist, &#8220;Kimi&#8221; masquerade ensemble in honor of André Sanou&#8217;s &#8216;Qui Dit Miuex?&#8217; (2022). Collection of Fitchburg Art Museum, photo courtesy of the New Orleans Museum of Art</figcaption></figure>



<p>&#8220;Across many West African cultures, masquerade a broad range of artistic, social, spiritual, and civic traditions,&#8221; the museum says. &#8220;Encompassing sculpture, textiles, performance, music, movement, and community participation, these performance traditions continuously adapt to contemporary life.&#8221; Sanou&#8217;s geometric masks are bold and brightly painted, often paired with costumes made from colorfully dyed fiber. And one can even spot pop culture references in Youmbi&#8217;s &#8220;Tso Scream Mask,&#8221; for example, which coats the iconic visage from the <em>Scream </em>movie franchise with thousands of beads.</p>



<p><em>New African Masquerades </em>is conceived as a dynamic exploration of the masquerade tradition&#8217;s collaborative and community-based practices, inviting viewers to a kind of reverie where time-honored heritage meets constant innovation. The show is organized by the New Orleans Museum of Art in partnership with the Museé des Civilisations noires in Dakar, Senegal. The exhibition opens on August 15 and continues through January 3, 2027, in St. Pete, Florida. Follow updates on the museum&#8217;s <a href="https://www.instagram.com/mfastpete/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img decoding="async" width="2000" height="3333" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-2.jpeg" alt="an elaborate and colorful African masquerade ensemble with beaded details and a face resembling the mask from 'Scream'" class="wp-image-476249" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-2.jpeg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-2-640x1067.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-2-960x1600.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-2-768x1280.jpeg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-2-922x1536.jpeg 922w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-2-1229x2048.jpeg 1229w" sizes="(max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Hervé Youmbi (Cameroon), &#8220;Tso Scream Mask&#8221; from the &#8216;Visage de masques (IX) series&#8217; (2015-2023), wood, pigment, fiber, beads, textile, glue, velvet fabric, cotton fabric, silk embroidery, and horse hair. Collection of the New Orleans Museum of Art</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img decoding="async" width="2000" height="1631" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-4.jpg" alt="an African masquerade ceremonial procession consisting of four figures in elaborate head-to-toe costumes" class="wp-image-476253" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-4.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-4-640x522.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-4-960x783.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-4-768x626.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-4-1536x1253.jpg 1536w" sizes="(max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Hervé Youmbi, &#8220;Tso Scream Mask&#8221; and &#8220;Tso Scream Leopard Mask&#8221; at the Nka&#8217;a Kossié society succession ceremony at Fondanti Chieftancy (December 3, 2022). Photo by Hervé Youmbi, courtesy of the artist and Axis Gallery, New York and New Jersey</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2512" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-7.jpeg" alt="an elaborate and colorful African masquerade ensemble" class="wp-image-476250" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-7.jpeg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-7-640x804.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-7-960x1206.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-7-768x965.jpeg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-7-1223x1536.jpeg 1223w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-7-1631x2048.jpeg 1631w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Sheku &#8220;Goldenfinger&#8221; Fofanah (Sierra Leone), &#8220;Fairy Masquerade Ensemble&#8221; (2022), fabric, sequins, wood, paint, and glue, life-size. Commission for the Fitchburg Art Museum, photo courtesy of the New Orleans Museum of Art</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1333" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-3.jpg" alt="Three figures dance in masks with long black braid-like ropes during a ceremony" class="wp-image-476252" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-3.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-3-640x427.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-3-960x640.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-3-768x512.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-3-1536x1024.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Hervé Youmbi, &#8220;Bamiléké-Kwele Ku&#8217;ngang Gorilla Mask&#8221; and &#8220;Single-faced Rhino Mask&#8221; during a ceremony in Fondanti village (2019). Photo by Hervé Youmbi, courtesy of the artist and Axis Gallery, New York and New Jersey</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1333" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-6.jpeg" alt="a photograph of geometric &quot;Kimi&quot; masks and colorful raffia costumes during a ceremonial performance" class="wp-image-476255" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-6.jpeg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-6-640x427.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-6-960x640.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-6-768x512.jpeg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-6-1536x1024.jpeg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Headpieces by David Sanou, studio of André Sanou, &#8220;Kimi&#8221; masks during a performance of greetings with the lead griot Tchiedo playing his drum behind them (May 3, 2022),  Bindougosso district, Bobo-Dioulasso, Burkina Faso. Photo by Lisa Homann</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2589" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-9.jpeg" alt="an elaborate African masquerade costume with white raffia ruffles and large armlets and anklets" class="wp-image-476257" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-9.jpeg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-9-640x828.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-9-960x1243.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-9-768x994.jpeg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-9-1187x1536.jpeg 1187w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-9-1582x2048.jpeg 1582w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Chief Ekpenyong Bassey Nsa (Nigeria), &#8220;Afia Awan Masquerade Ensemble&#8221; (2022), polyester fabric, raffia, and leather, life-size. Collection of the New Orleans Museum of Art</figcaption></figure>

Photo by Amanda M. Maples</figcaption></figure>

		<item>
		<title>Lucy Sparrow Invokes &#8217;90s Supermarket Nostalgia in ‘The Beginning of Convenience’</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/lucy-sparrow-the-beginning-of-convenience/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Jackie Andres]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Tue, 28 Jul 2026 20:11:28 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Craft]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[consumerism]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[felt]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[installation]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Lucy Sparrow]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[sewing]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[textiles]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=476119</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-10.jpg" alt="Lucy Sparrow Invokes &#8217;90s Supermarket Nostalgia in ‘The Beginning of Convenience’" />The artist's new exhibition is fully stocked with more than 20,000 handmade felt objects.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/lucy-sparrow-the-beginning-of-convenience/">Lucy Sparrow Invokes &#8217;90s Supermarket Nostalgia in ‘The Beginning of Convenience’</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-10.jpg" alt="Lucy Sparrow Invokes &#8217;90s Supermarket Nostalgia in ‘The Beginning of Convenience’" />


<p>Bentonville is a small town in Northwest Arkansas that has, over time, become synonymous with massive retail operations and corporate ecosystems. The bustling hub is ingrained with the legacy of <a href="https://downtownbentonville.org/go/the-walton-5-and-10" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Walton&#8217;s</a>, a small nickel and dime convenience store that opened on Bentonville&#8217;s downtown square in 1950 to serve its surrounding community. The shop quickly found success, and owner Sam Walton opened another store nearby that would evolve into the <a href="https://corporate.walmart.com/about/history" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">largest retailer</a> in the world: Walmart.</p>



<p>During this time and throughout the &#8217;60s, a post-war boom overtook the burgeoning commercial landscape of the United States. The suburban American Dream became a catalyst for retailers to adapt to an evolving social fabric that aimed to serve families hunting for necessities at an affordable price, and in a pinch. As a result, various amenities were introduced to convenience stores and chains, including the emergence of <a href="https://www.convenience.org/topics/fuels-and-energy/the-history-of-self-fueling" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">self-serve gasoline pumps</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1333" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-12.jpg" alt="a collection of handmade felt plush sculptures by Lucy Sparrow replicating a supermarket aisle stocked with various products and produce" class="wp-image-476178" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-12.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-12-640x427.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-12-960x640.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-12-768x512.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-12-1536x1024.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Installation view of &#8216;The Beginning of Convenience.&#8217; Photo by Wesley Hitt, courtesy of Getty Images for The Momentary</figcaption></figure>



<p>The 1980s and &#8217;90s, however, ushered in a new frontier of American commerce rooted in modernization. Supermarkets began to resemble the eptiome of a &#8220;one-stop-shop,&#8221; significantly transcending previous notions of convenience. In just one trip to the store, busy parents had the ability to pick out groceries for the week, restock housekeeping supplies, fill prescriptions, and feed their families lunch at the food court—all while waiting for their vacation photos to develop via <a href="https://www.nytimes.com/1988/02/06/business/rapid-rise-of-fast-photo-processing.html?unlocked_article_code=1.1FA.2GYn.1I9gFKNFfPHJ&amp;smid=url-share" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">rapid film processing</a>. Securing a quick and easy premade dinner was possible thanks to the popular frozen food aisle, and as a cherry on top, VHS movies were available for purchase to pair with the titular &#8220;<a href="https://www.smithsonianmag.com/arts-culture/brief-history-tv-dinner-180976039/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">TV dinner</a>.&#8221;</p>



<p>U.K.-based artist <a href="https://www.sewyoursoul.co.uk/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Lucy Sparrow</a> refers to this moment as &#8220;the beginning of convenience,&#8221; which doubles as the title of her newest large-scale installation and first museum exhibition in the United States. <em>The Beginning of Convenience</em> at <a href="https://themomentary.org/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">The Momentary</a> calls to the nostalgia of regional chain stores, retro packaging aesthetics, and a time when life was, as the artist described at the show&#8217;s opening, &#8220;becoming more about enjoyment and less about toil.&#8221;</p>



<p>For many, modern grocery stores can be imposing, and Sparrow&#8217;s monumental assemblage conjures a similar feeling of being carried away. The immensity of <em>The Beginning of Convenience</em>, however, invokes feelings of joy and comfort, rather than a newfangled sensory overload. Stocked to the brim with more than 20,000 handmade objects, an expansive collection of soft, felt artworks take over a 4,000-square-foot gallery space, creating an immersive experience for visitors—or, more fittingly—shoppers.</p>



<p>Much of the magic comes from the painstaking details that work together in molding an all-out sensory experience. For instance, as viewers weave through the aisles, music in the <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sXghfBU5EWY" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">style of old-school supermarket beats</a> hums in the background. The music however, is occasionally interrupted with amusing, familiar intercom announcements in a fuzzy tone, calling the parents or guardians of a lost young girl named Lucy to make their way to the photo department.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1333" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-1.jpg" alt="a collection of handmade felt plush sculptures by Lucy Sparrow replicating VHS tapes of iconic movies" class="wp-image-476167" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-1.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-1-640x427.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-1-960x640.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-1-768x512.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-1-1536x1024.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Installation view of &#8216;The Beginning of Convenience.&#8217; Photo by Wesley Hitt, courtesy of Getty Images for The Momentary</figcaption></figure>



<p>At the opening earlier this month, the artist was dressed for the occasion wearing a light blue, collared button-down shirtdress with vertical stripes running down the middle. Sparrow and her team shared that the custom garment was inspired by original Walmart uniforms from the company&#8217;s archives, extending a subtle nod to the fitting location of the exhibition.</p>



<p>Sparrow wields a remarkable ability to craft welcoming spaces for quite literally anyone. Each of the artist&#8217;s renowned <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/tags/lucy-sparrow/">installations over the years</a> are the brainchild of her own imaginative world, and a sense of vulnerability comes with our invitation into it. &#8220;Lucy’s work is quirky yet subversive,” says an exhibition statement. “Her soft and colorful felt creations charm and disarm visitors, while her detailed research practice and incisive observations inspire strong feelings of nostalgia, community, and conversations around shared history.”</p>



<p>This deeply humane feeling is refreshing within the context of American consumerism and growing corporatism. Especially as of late, the simple task of grocery shopping has become an increasingly divisive experience, and for many Americans, trips to the store are a looming reminder of shrinking household budgets and soaring prices, making it difficult to associate ordinary retail environments with anything but exhaustion or stress.</p>



<p>The presence of joy and childlike wonder in <em>The Beginning of Convenience</em> offers a significant subversion. Injecting this feeling into a visceral environment allows each viewer to shift their focus to enjoyment, the marvels of retail innovation, and the nostalgia that comes with it.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="960" height="1132" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lucy-jackiesphone-1-960x1132.jpg" alt="boxes of fruit with smiling faces" class="wp-image-476234" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lucy-jackiesphone-1-960x1132.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lucy-jackiesphone-1-640x755.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lucy-jackiesphone-1-768x905.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lucy-jackiesphone-1-1303x1536.jpg 1303w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lucy-jackiesphone-1-1737x2048.jpg 1737w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lucy-jackiesphone-1.jpg 2000w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 960px) 100vw, 960px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Installation view of &#8216;The Beginning of Convenience.&#8217; Photo by Jackie Andres</figcaption></figure>



<p>Evoking the emotional power of soft toys, felt as a material inspires feelings of warmth and security. While walking through Sparrow&#8217;s produce and meat department, this impression seems nearly impossible to ignore as netted bags of oranges, piles of juicy grapefruits, and fresh cuts of pork chop look up at you with shy smiles.</p>



<p>Because of this, it seems easy to tap into an imaginative world where many of Sparrow&#8217;s plush products unmistakably possess individual souls. Perhaps the Georgia peaches have a more bubbly personality than their spiky pineapple neighbors, and, conceivably, the beef steaks across the aisle may be tough on the outside but tender at heart. Somehow anything seems possible in a world that melds the energetic spirit of commercialism with the with the slow, mindful creation of the same objects through cutting, stuffing, sewing, and embellishing.</p>



<p>Upon exiting the supermarket experience, viewers encounter even more felt versions of common items within grocery store vestibules: vending machines dispensing your choice of Coke or Pepsi products, a photobooth, a coin-operated mechanical car ride, and an electronic ATM, which, at the time, was reaching its ubiquity.</p>



<p>Turning the corner into a separate area, visitors are met with a massive floor-to-ceiling installation of more than 3,000 stuffed bananas. The sight is a recreation of the artist&#8217;s &#8220;Banana Room,&#8221; a comforting place in her studio to relax and &#8220;be surrounded by happiness,&#8221; she says. Sparrow received her first plush banana when she was nine years old as a present from her father, and later received a larger version who was named Sebastian. Sebastian&#8217;s presence throughout the show and as a mascot for the artist&#8217;s practice is further proof of the unfaltering childlike wonder imbued within every corner of Sparrow&#8217;s practice.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1333" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-6.jpg" alt="Luct Sparrow sits in a room filled with thousands of bananas" class="wp-image-476172" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-6.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-6-640x427.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-6-960x640.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-6-768x512.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-6-1536x1024.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Lucy Sparrow at &#8216;The Beginning of Convenience.&#8217; Photo by Wesley Hitt, courtesy of Getty Images for The Momentary</figcaption></figure>



<p>Across from the Banana Room sits a replica of the &#8220;Felt Cave.&#8221; The space—previously an ambulance station that was converted into Sparrow&#8217;s Suffolk studio—offers more insight into her artistic process and the <a href="https://www.sewyoursoul.co.uk/inside-felt-hq/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">teamwork</a> that goes into creating thousands of objects, one at a time. Sparrow is supported by five full-time assistants, four cats, freelancers, and, of course, Sebastian.</p>



<p>Along with a faux window displaying the exact view from the studio—overlooking two colorful cars frequently parked outside, including a hot pink Jeep sporting a &#8220;F3LT U&#8221; license plate—The Felt Cave is filled with hundreds more surprises. As the exhibition label notes, there is &#8220;an &#8216;HR Department&#8217; of bespectacled bananas, a canary yellow cuckoo clock, and &#8216;dab dabs&#8217;—abstract paintings created from dabbing the excess off the tip of a paint bottle.&#8221;</p>



<p><em>The Beginning of Convenience</em> is on view through July 11, 2027. </p>



<figure class="wp-block-image"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1333" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-5.jpg" alt="a collection of handmade felt plush sculptures by Lucy Sparrow replicating a supermarket aisle stocked with various products and produce" class="wp-image-476171" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-5.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-5-640x427.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-5-960x640.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-5-768x512.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-5-1536x1024.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Installation view of &#8216;The Beginning of Convenience.&#8217; Photo by Wesley Hitt, courtesy of Getty Images for The Momentary</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1080" height="1350" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-15.jpg" alt="a collection of many handmade felt plush objects by Lucy Sparrow replicating packs of Hubba Bubba bubble gum" class="wp-image-476181" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-15.jpg 1080w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-15-640x800.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-15-960x1200.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-15-768x960.jpg 768w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1080px) 100vw, 1080px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Hubba Bubba,&#8221; 2026. Image courtesy of the artist</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="960" height="1280" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lucy-jackiesphone-4-960x1280.jpg" alt="" class="wp-image-476237" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lucy-jackiesphone-4-960x1280.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lucy-jackiesphone-4-640x853.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lucy-jackiesphone-4-768x1024.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lucy-jackiesphone-4-1152x1536.jpg 1152w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lucy-jackiesphone-4-1536x2048.jpg 1536w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lucy-jackiesphone-4.jpg 2000w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 960px) 100vw, 960px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Installation view of &#8216;The Beginning of Convenience.&#8217; Photo by Jackie Andres</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="960" height="720" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lucy-jackiesphone-3-960x720.jpg" alt="" class="wp-image-476236" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lucy-jackiesphone-3-960x720.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lucy-jackiesphone-3-640x480.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lucy-jackiesphone-3-768x576.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lucy-jackiesphone-3-1536x1152.jpg 1536w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lucy-jackiesphone-3.jpg 2000w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 960px) 100vw, 960px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Installation view of &#8216;The Beginning of Convenience.&#8217; Photo by Jackie Andres</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1333" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-4.jpg" alt="a collection of handmade felt plush sculptures by Lucy Sparrow replicating a supermarket aisle stocked with products with a wet floor sign in the shape of a banana" class="wp-image-476170" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-4.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-4-640x427.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-4-960x640.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-4-768x512.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sparrow-boc-4-1536x1024.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Installation view of &#8216;The Beginning of Convenience.&#8217; Photo by Wesley Hitt, courtesy of Getty Images for The Momentary</figcaption></figure>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/euro-3.jpeg" alt="Nature or Culture? Europeans Can Vote on the New Banknote Design" />Birds or figures? These are the ten design proposals for a new European banknote.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/euro-banknote-design-central-bank/">Nature or Culture? Europeans Can Vote on the New Banknote Design</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/euro-3.jpeg" alt="Nature or Culture? Europeans Can Vote on the New Banknote Design" />


<p>What best represents European life? The eternal dichotomy of nature vs. culture structures the Central Bank&#8217;s quest for a new banknote design, and now, the public can vote and offer feedback on ten proposals. </p>



<p>A panel of jurors selected the designs, which follow one of two themes: European places and ideas or birds and rivers, the latter of which is meant to symbolize freedom and unity. While the basic elements are the same—all collections devoted to culture feature the same six figures, including Renaissance artist Leonardo da Vinci, composer Ludwig van Beethoven, scientist Marie Curie, opera singer Maria Callas, and authors Bertha von Suttner and Miguel de Cervantes, for example—individual approaches appear in the layout, aesthetic, and composition.</p>



<p>Voting is open through mid-September, when jurors will select one design that will go through an additional vetting process before the organization adopts it entirely. View all ten on <a href="https://www.ecb.europa.eu/euro/banknotes/future_banknotes/html/all-design-proposals.en.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">the bank&#8217;s website</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1177" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/euro-4.jpg" alt="a collection of potential designs for euros" class="wp-image-476224" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/euro-4.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/euro-4-640x377.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/euro-4-960x565.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/euro-4-768x452.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/euro-4-1536x904.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Rudy Guedj and François Girard-Meunier</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1215" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/euro-5.jpg" alt="a collection of potential designs for euros" class="wp-image-476226" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/euro-5.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/euro-5-640x389.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/euro-5-960x583.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/euro-5-768x467.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/euro-5-1536x933.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Neue Gestaltung GmbH</figcaption></figure>

		<item>
		<title>&#8216;Colorstruck!&#8217; Examines the Connection Between Race and Chromatic Expression</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/richard-j-powell-black-american-art-colorstruck/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Grace Ebert]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Mon, 27 Jul 2026 20:26:58 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Books]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[History]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[art history]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[color]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[identity]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[painting]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[portraits]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=476206</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-2.jpg" alt="&#8216;Colorstruck!&#8217; Examines the Connection Between Race and Chromatic Expression" />'Colorstruck! Painting, Pigment, Affect' delves into the ways that color and social, political, and cultural forces intersect in Black American art.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/richard-j-powell-black-american-art-colorstruck/">&#8216;Colorstruck!&#8217; Examines the Connection Between Race and Chromatic Expression</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-2.jpg" alt="&#8216;Colorstruck!&#8217; Examines the Connection Between Race and Chromatic Expression" />


<p>A nude Black woman lies on a stark white chaise, her head propped up by her thin arm. She&#8217;s surrounded by flat, abstracted color in the form of fruits and fabrics, and a glass coupe and bottle on a nearby table offer a clear, rather than refracted, view of the vibrant scene. Rendered in oil on burlap, the painting by William H. Johnson is commanding in its palette and subject matter and an exemplary work in a new book by art historian <a href="https://richardjpowell.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Richard J. Powell</a>.</p>



<p>Forthcoming this fall from Princeton University Press, <a href="https://bookshop.org/a/96/9780691285160" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener"><em>Colorstruck! Painting, Pigment, Affect</em></a> delves into the ways that color and social, political, and cultural forces intersect in Black American art. Powell takes an expansive approach to each of the three topics—painting, pigment, and affect—and examines works by a wide group of artists, including Jacob Lawrence, Alma Thomas, <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/tags/lorna-simpson/">Lorna Simpson</a>, <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/tags/jean-michel-basquiat/">Jean-Michel Basquiat</a>, and <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/tags/nina-chanel-abney/">Nina Chanel Abney</a>. His interest is in the dynamic interplay of paint and pigment and what the two reveal about both the artists and the viewers.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1514" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-3.jpg" alt="a stylized painted portrait of a nude Black woman" class="wp-image-476210" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-3.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-3-640x484.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-3-960x727.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-3-768x581.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-3-1536x1163.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">William H. Johnson, &#8220;Nude&#8221; (c. 1939), oil on burlap, 29 ¾ x 38 ¼ inches. Image courtesy of Smithsonian American Art Museum and Art Resource</figcaption></figure>



<p>Sharing a root with words like awestruck or starstruck, <em>colorstruck</em> is a slang term that evolved from &#8220;a Black person who preferred associating with light-skinned Blacks or White people to anyone inordinately preoccupied with race,&#8221; Powell writes. The idea is largely associated with colorism, although in his view, it can also be applied to the ways we marvel at and can even be overwhelmingly affected by an artist&#8217;s palette. He adds: </p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p>What if a painter, like early Black modernist Willian H. Johnson, set aside the more pejorative insinuations in the idea of being <em>colorstruck</em>, and instead used the paint medium, an intense color palette, racial Blackness, and most important, his abstracting inclinations to produce an expressionistic, evocative, and disruptive work of art? </p>
</blockquote>



<p>The book continues in this line of thinking as it connects what is often thought of as a universal concept—that color exists, and humans respond to certain hues in particular ways—and the distinct context of race in America. Richly illustrated with archival photographs and numerous artworks, the volume captures the relationship between the unique experience of an artist and her viewer and the broader powers that inform those dynamics.</p>



<p><em>Colorstruck! Painting, Pigment, Affect</em> will be published in September, and you can pre-order your copy through <a href="https://bookshop.org/a/96/9780691285160" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Bookshop</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2733" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-1.jpg" alt="an abstract print" class="wp-image-476208" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-1.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-1-640x875.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-1-960x1312.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-1-768x1049.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-1-1124x1536.jpg 1124w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-1-1499x2048.jpg 1499w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Hervé Télémaque, &#8220;Négrerie (Black cultural effects)&#8221; (1974), lithograph, 30 x 22 inches. Image © The Metropolitan Museum of Art, courtesy of Art Resource</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2458" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-4.jpg" alt="an abstract painting of color fields" class="wp-image-476211" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-4.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-4-640x787.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-4-960x1180.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-4-768x944.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-4-1250x1536.jpg 1250w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-4-1666x2048.jpg 1666w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Alma Thomas, &#8220;The Eclipse&#8221; (1970), acrylic on canvas, 62 x 49 ¾ inches. Image courtesy of Smithsonian American Art Museum and Art Resource</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2002" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-5.jpg" alt="a small figure in white against a vast orange backdrop" class="wp-image-476212" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-5.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-5-640x641.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-5-960x961.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-5-150x150.jpg 150w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-5-768x769.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-5-1534x1536.jpg 1534w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Malcolm Bailey, &#8220;Untitled&#8221; (1972), cut and pasted paper and acrylic on Plexiglas, 36 x 36 inches. Image copyright © The Metropolitan Museum of Art, courtesy of Art Resource</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2548" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-6.jpg" alt="a painted portrait of a Black woman" class="wp-image-476213" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-6.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-6-640x815.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-6-960x1223.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-6-768x978.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-6-1206x1536.jpg 1206w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/colorstruck-6-1608x2048.jpg 1608w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Charles Alston, &#8220;Girl in a Red Dress&#8221; (1934), oil on canvas, 28 x 22 inches. Image © The Metropolitan Museum of Art, courtesy of Art Resource</figcaption></figure>
